title: Telling people to hit Ctrl+Alt+F1 when the screen locker is broken is not always (or ever?) accurate
line: When the screen locker breaks, its message now tells you to press Ctrl+Alt+F3 to reach a text console instead of F1 or F2.
explanation: The emergency screen shown when the greeter keeps crashing picked VT 2, or VT 1 if the session was on VT 2. On most distros those are the display manager or the graphical session itself, so pressing the suggested keys froze the screen or showed an empty console, as the reporter and Nate saw (F3 is the one that works). The message now suggests VT 3, or VT 4 when the session itself runs on VT 3, which logind gives a login prompt by default.

commits.message:
emergencywindow: suggest Ctrl+Alt+F3 to reach a text console

The broken locker message suggested switching to VT 1 or 2, but those
usually hold the display manager or the graphical session, so users got
a frozen or empty screen. Suggest VT 3 instead, or 4 if we run on it.

BUG: 473247

media.caption: Master: the emergency screen suggests Ctrl+Alt+F2
With the fix: it suggests Ctrl+Alt+F3

review.text: Clean and minimal fix in kscreenlocker that switches the emergency recovery screen suggestion from VT 1/2 to VT 3 (with VT 4 as fallback when the session runs on VT 3) for both ConsoleKit and logind. It reuses the existing translated placeholders with no string churn and matches the bug report's direction. Before/after screenshots and passing autotests verify the change.

reviews.text: Clean and minimal fix in kscreenlocker that switches the emergency recovery screen suggestion from VT 1/2 to VT 3 (with VT 4 as fallback when the session runs on VT 3) for both ConsoleKit and logind. It reuses the existing translated placeholders with no string churn and matches the bug report's direction. Before/after screenshots and passing autotests verify the change.

Switching the suggested VT from 1/2 to 3 (4 if the session is on 3) fixes the reporter's case and matches what Nate and c6 found working, in the right place and without new strings. But bug 466178 ('recovery advice doesn't make sense when there are no VTs') was merged into this one in May 2026, and that half is untouched: with XDG_VTNR unset the message still says to switch back with Ctrl+Alt+F0, which the fix's own after-1.png shows (and verify waves off as a rig artifact). As it stands the commit would close a bug whose merged duplicate is still visibly wrong.
changes: Handle XDG_VTNR being unset/0: don't print 'Ctrl+Alt+F0' for getting back to the session (e.g. a variant without the back key, or advise 'loginctl activate <session>'), so the no-VT case from the merged 466178 is covered too.

Likewise avoid printing a bare 'loginctl unlock-session' when XDG_SESSION_ID is empty (run from the VT it would target the wrong session); fall back to telling the user to find it with 'loginctl list-sessions'.
Since the VT is still a guess per distro (Nate c3), consider wording like 'e.g. Ctrl+Alt+F3, or another F key if that shows nothing'.
Verify the VT 3 -> F4 branch and the no-VT text, with screenshots of each.
